newsitem.title: INDIA: Highlights of changes in Indian tax proposals.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of changes in Indian tax proposals.

text.p: Following are the highlights of changes in tax proposals which Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced on Wednesday after moving the Finance Bill for 1996/97 (April-March).
The changes in customs and excise duties would involve a net revenue loss of 940 million rupees to the government, he said.
--Profits of "sick", or ailing, industrial units and of firms located in backward districts or states excluded from minimum alternate tax (MAT).
--Customs duty on colour picture tubes increased to 35 percent from 30 percent.
--Customs duty on primary forms of stainless steel other than stainless steel slabs increased to 30 per cent from 20 per cent.
--Customs duty on stainless steel scrap reduced to 10 per cent from 20 per cent.
--Customs duty on rayon grade wood pulp reduced to 10 per cent from 25 per cent.
--Customs duty on hard-disk drives, floppy disk drives and Compact Disc-Read Only Memory (CD-ROM) drives reduced to 10 percent from 20 percent.
--Customs duty on methanol brought down to 30 per cent from 40 per cent, and on epichlorohydrin to 30 percent from 40 percent.
--Long-term capital gains tax for partnership firms and association of persons reduced from to 20 percent from 30.
--Income Tax Act amended to reduce definition of time period of long-term finance to five years from seven years.
--Commercial properties forming part of stock-in-trade exempted from wealth tax.
--Spoons, forks and some other items exempted from excise duty.
--Absorbent and non-absorbent cotton wool, gauze, bandages and similar medical articles without brand names exempted from excise duty.
--Excise on insulated wares of plastic reduced to 15 percent from 20 percent.
--Unprocessed knitted or crocheted fabrics of man-made fibre as well as certain specified processed narrow woven fabrics of cotton and man-made fibres exempted from excise duty.
